name: Mustilli Sant'Agata dei Goti (Greco di Tufo)
tasting_notes: Bright and refreshing, this offers aromas of orchard fruit and citrus. The lively palate delivers white peach, mature pear and nectarine alongside crisp acidity while a mineral note signals the close.

name: Barton & Guestier Thomas Barton Réserve Privé (Médoc)
tasting_notes: While the aromas speak of wood aging, the fruit comes through on the palate. It is firm, full and dry, and the fruity acidity and fresh black currant flavor backs up the structure.

name: Tsantali Réserve Agiorgitiko (Nemea)
tasting_notes: Agiorgitiko, famed in Nemea and popular for its soft, fragrant red berry character, is represented well in this balanced, flavorful wine. A nose of wooded spice, pepper and Mediterranean herbs is followed by waves of soft tannis, red fruit, spice and a touch of smoke. Pair with steak or a meat stew.

name: Bodega Norton Chardonnay (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Could the scent of microwaved popcorn be any stronger? Obviously, it's heavily oaked, and that carries onto the palate where you'll find heavy, woody flavors in addition to banana and lemon. This needs a lot more charm and style; in all honesty, it's not delivering much.

name: Maurice Ecard Les Serpentières Premier Cru (Savigny-lès-Beaune)
tasting_notes: Soft and ripe, this is a broad wine. Its tannins are enveloped by the rich plum and damson fruit flavors. It combines the richness of the vintage with the softness of a Savigny in an already delicious whole.

name: Château du Moulin Rouge Haut-Médoc
tasting_notes: Fresh and fruity, this wine is full of black currants and acidity that is structured by a core of dark tannins. While it is firm at the moment it's likely to fill out, with the fresh fruitiness emerging. Drink from 2017.

name: Fattoria di Grignano Vin Santo del Chianti Rufina
tasting_notes: This rich dessert nectar from Tuscany is made from a blend of Trebbiano and Malvasia grapes. It delivers typical Vin Santo aromas and flavors of maple syrup, dried apricot and candied oranges. Dense and sweet, it's a perfect match for traditional cantucci biscuits or to sip on its own after dinner.

name: Quinta de Sant'Ana Reserva Red (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: A serious, powerful and rich wine, it has great structure that is allied with ripe black plum fruits and a dense texture. Since the structure and fruit balance, the wine is drinkable now, although it is also likely to age. Drink before 2020.

name: Tasca d'Almerita Sallier de la Tour Inzolia (Sicilia)
tasting_notes: Spicy, fresh and clean, this would pair with fried seafood or spaghetti con vongole. It offers pretty citrus tones followed by a drying mineral nuance.

name: Simone Grand Reserve Red (Maule Valley)
tasting_notes: Meaty and leathery on first blush, with chunky dark-fruit aromas leading to a beefy palate with pure plum and blackberry flavors. Thick, layered and relatively deep, with a good DNA and commendable purity and overall quality. Very close to top-level Cab from Chile, with 15% Carmenère and 5% Petit Verdot.

name: Pietro Rinaldi Monvigliero (Barolo)
tasting_notes: Crisp and slender, this offers drying tannins and aromas of fresh berry and white cherry. It shows a subdued and elegant personality overall.

name: Vicente Gandia El Miracle 120 Tempranillo-Shiraz (Valencia)
tasting_notes: Leathery plum and berry aromas come with a touch of char. This blend of Shiraz and Tempranillo feels round and solid. Familiar flavors of berry fruits and cherry are a bit spicy, while the finish tastes of black fruits and feels right.

name: Perticaia Montefalco Sagrantino
tasting_notes: This opens with aromas reminiscent of stewed plum, dark culinary spice, espresso and a balsamic note. The assertive palate is still tightly wound, offering dried black cherry, raisin, licorice and tobacco set against taut, close-grained tannins. Drink 2020–2028.

name: Chateau Mourgues du Gres Les Galets Dorés White (Costières de Nîmes)
tasting_notes: This mildly aromatic blend of Grenache Blanc, Roussanne and Vermentino marries apple and lime flavors into a fresh, citrusy white that persists nicely on the finish. Drink now.

name: Colterenzio Puiten Pinot Grigio (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: Puiten is a slightly wider and creamier expression compared to the estate's base Pinot Grigio. The wine shows pretty aromas of peach and citrus as well as a very thick and succulent feel in the mouth.

name: Valle dell'Acate Case Ibidini Syrah (Sicilia)
tasting_notes: Here's a young, fruity and easygoing expression of Syrah with aromas of crushed blueberries and chalky mineral nuances. The wine has good density and berry flavors, making for an approachable and correct companion to stay-home dinners.

name: Quinta das Arcas Arca Nova Colheita Loureiro (Vinho Verde)
tasting_notes: Made from one of the star grapes of Vinho Verde, this is a ripe, creamy wine. It has hints of lemon zest, along with grapefruit and a herbal aftertaste. It is crisp and ready to drink.

name: Valentin Bianchi Famiglia Bianchi Malbec (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Pencil eraser, iodine, latex and blueberry aromas settle better than they start. In the mouth, this is saturated and chunky in feel, with toasty flavors of blackberry, licorice and mint that finish long, herbal and loamy.

name: Cono Sur 20 Barrels Limited Edition Pinot Noir (Casablanca Valley)
tasting_notes: This mature PN from a hot vintage isn't showing much life. Earthy, raisiny aromas aren't fresh, while wood tannin and acid are keeping it afloat. Flavors of brown sugar and decayed berry fruits finish stale. This is on its very last legs.

name: Arunda Brut Sparkling (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: Using the Metodo Classico, this shows bright aromas of citrus, mountain flower and apricot. The mouthfeel is round and smooth, with a playful touch of bitter almond on the close.

name: Con un Par Albariño (Rías Baixas)
tasting_notes: This quiet Albariño comes from the Vicente Gandia family of wines. It opens with short, peppery aromas backed by a medium-bodied palate. Peppery, slightly bitter flavors echo the nose, with a hint of stone fruit to help it along. Drink now.

name: Viña Requingua Toro de Piedra Grand Reserve Merlot (Curicó Valley)
tasting_notes: Dry, spicy berry aromas are pedestrian but fine. This is tight, fresh and a touch scraping on the palate, with plum, currant and roasted flavors. Spicy, minty and solid on the finish, this is a perfectly good Merlot with limitations.

name: Coto de Hayas Garnacha-Syrah (Campo de Borja)
tasting_notes: Common cherry and berry aromas lead to a fruit-punch palate with some stickiness. This tastes ripe, with nothing distinguished beyond basic berry flavors. Sweet plum and berry notes steer the finish.

name: Aresti Estate Selection Sauvignon Blanc (Curicó Valley)
tasting_notes: Plump but wholly generic, with semisweet aromas that are neither here nor there. The palate is round, with adequate to good mouthfeel. And the flavors of citrus are solid but kind of pithy and bitter. A full, chunky wine with virtues as well as some flaws. Drink right away for best results.

name: Château Plaisance Cuvée Alix (Bordeaux Blanc)
tasting_notes: A wine that is, unusually for Bordeaux, dominated by Sémillon. That gives a creamy, ripe and still muted character and demands another few years aging. The acidity and fresh citrus fruits are filled out with melon and ripe pear flavors. Drink this wine from 2016.

name: Lohsa Morellino di Scansano
tasting_notes: Fresh and full, with a deep berry nose, drying tannins and ample but not overdone oak. In the mouth, it's pretty solid, and the cherry and black-plum fruit is clean and tasty. It's on the stout side, with youthful acidity and a good deal of warmth to the smoky finish. From Poliziano.

name: Château Durfort-Vivens Margaux
tasting_notes: Made in a firm, solid style, this wine shows considerable potential. Pure berry flavors are prominent along with the dense tannins. It is a good wine for the difficult vintage and will be ready to drink from 2020. The estate is in the process of converting to biodynamic methods.

name: Joseph Cattin Hatschbourg Grand Cru Trésor des Seigneurs Pinot Gris (Alsace)
tasting_notes: Named after the lords of Hattstatt—a word that evolved to Hatschbourg—this wine comes from selected grapes. It's a medium sweet, rich wine with a smooth structure and opulent texture. Lychees and yellow fruits are cut with lime acidity to balance ripeness and freshness. It's a wine to age, drink from 2018.

name: Château de Fontenille Entre-Deux-Mers
tasting_notes: Rich and fruity, this wine shows warm white fruit and a touch of spice. The wine is soft, its currant and pink grapefruit flavors lifted by acidity but with a rounded finish.

name: Emiliana Eco Balance Carmenère (Colchagua Valley)
tasting_notes: Earthy and mossy smelling, which is true to the variety. In addition, there's mild balsamic and dark-berry aromas. The palate is full and easy, with black-fruit flavors that carry herb and peppery qualities. Sweet and sizable for a $9 wine, with toast, coffee and controlled bitterness on the finish.

name: Tritón Old Vines (Toro)
tasting_notes: Aromas of oak, asphalt, and ripe black fruits make for a lusty, modern nose. The feel is jammy and thick. Flavors of blackberry, chocolate and mocha give way to a strong oak component. A dense finish runs minty and chocolaty, with an emphasis on syrupy richness. Drink through 2021.

name: Vino San Esteban Réserve Malbec
tasting_notes: A French version of a brand that is more familiar in Chile as Viña San Esteban, this wine has more stylistically to do with South America than southwest France. It is soft, juicy, rounded and with attractive ripe tannins. The wine is ready to drink.

name: Budini Chardonnay (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Two vintages ago this wine rated the same, so we can say that improvement and evolution are not evident. This wine is tan in color and heavy, with strange butterscotch aromas that seem foreign and artificial. Forced oak flavors and a resiny mouthfeel are also drawbacks.

name: Atipax Reserva Red (Tupungato)
tasting_notes: Deep purple in color, and soupy on the nose, with a strong hint of lemon. The palate is almost astringent due to elevated acidity, thus the balance of this Malbec-Cabernet Sauvignon-Bonarda blend is sketchy. Tastes more like grape juice than fine wine, with a hollow, tangy finish.

name: Marrenon Grande Toque Rosé (Luberon)
tasting_notes: This pale-hued blend of Grenache and Syrah starts off a bit confected, offering up scents of cotton candy. Yet it's less so on the palate, where the fruit resembles underripe melon and the finish is stony and less generous.

name: Doña Paula Los Cardos Malbec (Luján de Cuyo)
tasting_notes: Big and fruity, and for the most part holds together and exhibits more good qualities than its faults. The flavor profile drives full-bodied black fruit and a finish that cuts out quietly. Not over the top in any way.

name: Eduardo Garrido García Gran Reserva (Rioja)
tasting_notes: Strawberry and raspberry aromas are a touch briny. This is lively in the mouth, with lasting acidity that offers kick to an aged Rioja. Spicy notes of pepper sit on top of base-level cherry and plum fruit, while toast and spice flavors along with lasting acidity drive the finish.

name: Wolfberger Pinot Blanc (Alsace)
tasting_notes: Soft and ripe, this is an attractive, light and fragrant wine. There is a good strand of acidity that runs through the wine, giving a counterpoint to the apple and spice flavors. Drink now.

name: Henri Bourgeois Les Baronnes (Sancerre)
tasting_notes: This is a lighter style of Pinot Noir than some produced in Sancerre today. It brings out perfumes and red-cherry flavors lifted by acidity. The wine is fruity, with hints of wood aging and a juicy aftertaste. Drink now.

name: Dr. Heidemanns-Bergweiler Dry Riesling (Mosel)
tasting_notes: Scents of fresh apple and pear are accented with touches of wax and mineral on this nuanced, dry Riesling. The palate feels lush and fruity with ripe peach and pear flavors, but zesty lime acidity and a shower of minerality lend stately elegance. A surprisingly bold wine for a diminutive price. Drink now.

name: Castello del Poggio Brachetto (Piedmont)
tasting_notes: This is a sweet, rosé -colored sparkling wine (made from the Brachetto grape) with bright aromas of wild berry and peach. This particular wine also boasts soft foaming and a playful touch of ripe cherry on the close.

name: Bodega Atamisque Catalpa Single Vineyard Chardonnay (Tupungato)
tasting_notes: Chunky, oxidized aromas announce a wine that's past its prime. A globular, round mouthfeel lacks definition, while flavors of caramel and oxidized stone fruits finish woody, toasty and bitter.

name: Quinta do Passadouro Passadouro Touriga Franca (Douro)
tasting_notes: The Touriga Franca is the most widely planted red vine in the Douro, giving, as here, a ripe and fruity wine that is full of red fruits that come right to the fore. The tannins are there in background to give the structure, while it is the exuberant fruit and acidity that dominate. Drink from 2018.

name: Katunar Kvalitetno Vino Vinogorje Zlahtina (Krk)
tasting_notes: Light yellow in color, this has heady aromas of elderflower, white lemon blossom and freshly picked basil. There are touches of vanilla and honeycomb on the palate, with fresh stone fruit flavors. It's well-balanced, with an energetic acidic finish.

name: Graci Arcurìa Bianco (Etna)
tasting_notes: Made with 100% native grape Carricante, this offers delicate aromas of honeysuckle, broom, brimstone and a note of stone fruit. The vertical palate offers green apple, citrus peel, mineral and rosemary, while aging in casks adds a layer of complexity. It's impeccably balanced with bright acidity.

name: Domaine de Nizas Rosé (Coteaux du Languedoc)
tasting_notes: The nose offers minor essences of apple core and more pronounced notes of wet minerality. On the palate, more refreshingly acidic characteristics shine with flavors of ripe rhubarb and red cherry. A rosé perfectly designed for enjoying with food.

name: Les Vignerons Réunis de Monségur Château Grand Billard (Bordeaux)
tasting_notes: Young and fruity, this is an attractive red- and black-currant-flavored wine. Its youthful stalky character will soften quickly to highlight the fruit. Drink from late 2016.

name: Wines & Winemakers Azul Portugal Spumante Bruto Sparkling (Bairrada)
tasting_notes: The blend of Bical and Arinto is typical of the sparkling wines from the Bairrada region. Together they give a crisp style of wine, bright with acidity and tangy with citrus and orange peel. The wine is ready to drink.

name: Left Bend Camel Hill Cabernet Sauvignon (Santa Cruz)
tasting_notes: The nose is somewhat reserved on this wine from the stylish brand Left Bend, named after the San Andreas Fault, though cherry liqueur, plum jam and red clay do emerge. The scents translate to vivid flavors, though, with cinnamon spice, ollallieberry and black pepper on the palate.

name: Tinhof Tinhof Noir Red (Burgenland)
tasting_notes: There is more fruit than structure in this wine, giving the palate a bright, red-berried character and soft tannins. It's juicy, but there's also some smokiness. A blend of Zweigelt, Blaufränkisch and St Laurent, it is ready to drink now. Screwcap.

name: Zlatan Otok Plavac Mali (North Dalmatia)
tasting_notes: Bright cherry, red plum and vanilla notes are well pronounced in the nose and on the palate. There's a touch of cherry-vanilla soda as well. The finish pops with a bright persistence of fruit.

name: Echeverria Carmenère (Central Valley)
tasting_notes: Welcoming jammy fruit aromas are clean and robust, while the palate on this value-priced bottling is creamy, balanced and generous. The flavors are naturally a bit herbal, but there's so much beefy blackberry and dark plum fruit that the package is downright commendable. For everyday Carmenère, this is where to look.

name: Tamaya Reserva Viognier-Chardonnay White (Limarí Valley)
tasting_notes: Lazy smelling, oddly spiced and off the grid in an artificial, strange sort of way. Flavors of apple, spice and banana are mulled and cidery, while the finish is grabby and hot. Not as good as prior vintages. Imported by Ecovalley Quality Wine Group and National Refrescos Import Company, LLC.

name: Domaine Sorin Terra Amata Rosé (Côtes de Provence)
tasting_notes: From vineyards near Bandol, close to the Mediterranean coast, this full and fruity wine has a lighter side with its fresh acidity. Red berry flavors are cut with a lemon zest texture, the aftertaste bright and refreshing with its acidity. The blend is 30% Grenache, 20% Syrah, 15% Cinsault, 15% Mourvèdre, 15% Carignan, 10% Rolle and 2% Ugni Blanc.

name: Collovray et Terrier Vieilles Vignes (Saint-Véran)
tasting_notes: The wine is closed, but has potential. At the moment, the wood and texture dominate, but there are signs of ripe apple and pear fruits that will come through in a few months. Wait until the end of 2014.

name: Cantina Terlano Pinot Grigio (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: White wildflower and Bosc pear aromas lead the nose. The bright, linear palate offers nectarine zest and crisp Granny Smith alongside zesty acidity. A mineral note closes the tangy finish.

name: Château Philippe-le-Hardi La Brigadière Vieilles Vignes (Mercurey)
tasting_notes: This is an earthy wine that shows a rustic character. Still youthful, its fruit is obscured behind a dry, tannic, burnt-toast character. There is a future for this wine, as it should integrate with age, so don't try to drink until 2016.

name: Bodegas Faustino Faustino V Rosado Tempranillo (Rioja)
tasting_notes: Dusty and still fairly fresh, but with that said this wine was certainly more in its prime six or eight months ago. Now it is slick but softening, with peach and citrus flavors doing their thing without much edge or kick.

name: La Bouvaude Elégance Red (Côtes du Rhône)
tasting_notes: Plush and creamy in texture, loaded up with toasted coconut and vanilla, this is a tasty, well crafted oaky red. Hints of berries add depth to the vanilla-laden palate, then linger on the supple finish. Drink now.

name: Los Nevados Malbec (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Opens with gumball aromas and also foresty spice and bramble. The palate is tight and tannic as it delivers standard red licorice, berry and leathery flavors. Finishes with some salty leather and that's about it.

name: William Fèvre Domaine (Chablis)
tasting_notes: For simple Chablis, this is impressive, rich, fruity, with wood as well as lively, fresh acidity. Nosings find toast and butter, with a hint of light honey.

name: Finca Flichman Paisaje de Tupungato Malbec (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Coffee, beef stock, blackberry and graphite aromas require patience to process. A lively, ringing palate is jammy at its essence. Dark, toasty flavors of blackberry and blueberry are mildly green and herbal. It feels rubbery on a tannic finish.

name: Valdelacierva Crianza (Rioja)
tasting_notes: Cherry, plum, vanilla and mild oak aromas feed into a medium-bodied, elegant palate with plum and cherry flavors supported by a touch of toasty oak and vanilla. Notes of café mocha and toast grace a crisp finish that isn't trying too hard.

name: Torre di Luna Sauvignon (Delle Venezie)
tasting_notes: Torre di Luna is an Italian brand you can count on for value and good cheer. This offers crisp aromas of citrus and tomato leaf, followed by a fresh mouthfeel.

name: Feudi di San Gregorio Campanaro White (Irpinia)
tasting_notes: The two grapes that represent the pride of southern Italian winemaking—Fiano and Greco—are blended here to produce a creamy, rich white wine that will pair well with steamed lobster or crab. Beautifully balanced sensations of acidity and spice appear on the long finish.

name: Castello di Monsanto 50th Harvest Riserva (Chianti Classico)
tasting_notes: Fragrant and elegantly structured, this blend of Sangiovese and 10% Canaiolo and Colorino opens with lovely aromas of pressed violet, iris, perfumed berry and baking spice. On the palate, notes of white pepper, toast, espresso and anise accent the black cherry core. Tightly knit but polished tannins give it a firm finish. Drink 2016–2022.

name: Michel Torino Ciclos Malbec-Merlot (Cafayate)
tasting_notes: The nose on this Malbec-Merlot blend starts off charred and leathery, but with airing you'll get roasted berry fruit scents and mild stalky characteristics. Flavors of roasted berries, rubber and leather finish loud, with muscular tannins and blazing acidity.

name: Blanco Nieva Verdejo (Rueda)
tasting_notes: This is waxy on the nose, with the aromatic spunk of nettle and sweaty citrus. It feels fresh, minerally and zesty, with citrus, apple and green herb flavors. It's solid, smooth and elegant on the finish, which turns slightly bitter as it concludes.

name: Château d'Arce Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux
tasting_notes: This wine is soft, open and full of fruit. It has a tang of acidity as well as rich berry flavors and a supporting layer of tannin. Fine, smoky and structured, it will be easy to drink from 2019.

name: Merotto Colbello Extra Dry (Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore)
tasting_notes: Delicate aromas of spring flowers and white stone fruit lead the nose. The palate offers crisp green apple, yellow pear and creamy white peach alongside refreshing acidity and a foaming mousse.

name: Luis Felipe Edwards Family Selection Cabernet Sauvignon (Colchagua Valley)
tasting_notes: Cassis, black cherry and other solid dark-fruit aromas seem solid and inviting. The palate is saturated but shows good texture and flow, while the flavors and essence of cassis, raspberry and eucaplytus are ingrained all the way to the finish. Springy, tasty and attractive, but not complicated.

name: I Sodi Riserva (Chianti Classico)
tasting_notes: Intensely floral, this opens with aromas of blue iris, crushed violet, ripe berry and a whiff of baking spice. The elegantly structured palate doles out juicy plum, ripe wild cherry, vanilla, cinnamon and mocha accompanied by fine-grained tannins. Drink through 2021.

name: Martín Berdugo Verdejo (Rueda)
tasting_notes: Floral aromas mixed with citrus notes are appealing. This wine feels round but solidified by bright core acidity. Ripe flavors include pineapple, mango and peach. On the finish, lime and tropical notes are good but short.

name: Château Eugénie Cuvée Réserve de l'Aïeul Malbec-Tannat (Cahors)
tasting_notes: With its spice and mint aromas, this wine shows its 30% new wood aging strongly. On the palate, the mint flavors balance with rich black fruit and a strong, firmly tannic backbone. Rich and full of potential, it will be ready to drink from 2020.

name: Christophe Cordier Clos du Four (Mâcon-Milly Lamartine)
tasting_notes: In this ripe wine, yellow fruits, cinnamon and ripe herbs are melded into a harmonious whole. Great acidity offers a juicy core to this well-balanced wine. Drink now for its great refreshing character.

name: I Capitani Bosco Faiano (Taurasi)
tasting_notes: Here's a traditional, old school Taurasi with bright notes of apple skin and red berry that add buoyancy and freshness. The wine is drinkable and approachable (not always an easy feat for Aglianico) and leaves a long endnote of dusty tannins.

name: Château La Greffière Mâcon-Milly Lamartine
tasting_notes: This attractive wine offers lemon and sliced-apple fruitiness. It has a lively character, crisp, tangy and ready to drink.

name: Rexach Baqués Brut Imperial Reserva Sparkling (Cava)
tasting_notes: Floral lime aromas are fresh, while this wine feels tight, and light. Bright citrus and tropical-fruit flavors are winners, and this is steady and fresh on a tasty finish.

name: Le Cirque Rosé (Côtes Catalanes)
tasting_notes: Forward scents of white raspberry, muddled cherry, pressed pink flowers and white chocolate suggest this is a ripe and rich rosé. The round palate is surprisingly juxtaposed by a sharp astringency that dominates through the finish.

name: Quinta do Casal Monteiro Red (Tejo)
tasting_notes: This wine is a blend of Touriga Nacional, Merlot and Syrah, giving fruit, fresh berry flavors and acidity. It has some structure, showing a dry background to the forward juicy flavors. It should be better in a year, so drink from 2016.

name: Purcari Freedom Blend Red (Moldova)
tasting_notes: Bright ruby in the glass, this wine is a blend of the Bastardo grape with indigenous varieties Saperavi and Rara Neagra. It offers a fruit-forward bouquet of cherry and blackberry. On the palate, flavors of freshly picked plum and black cherry with a touch of green pepper are sheathed in a lattice of supple tannins.

name: Cantina Produttori Bolzano S. Maddalena/Gries Dellago Pinot Bianco (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: This cool-climate expression shows exceptionally-beautiful tones of peach, melon and pear. A tiny percentage of the wine is aged in French barrel. This is a fantastic white wine to pair with fish, white meat or vegetables..

name: Ruca Malen Reserva Petit Verdot (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Dry spicy aromas accent woodsy berry scents. A tight focused palate jabs with acidity and poking tannins, while this tastes of lightly herbal cherry and berry fruit. Spicy flavors on a healthy finish help this along.

name: Les Vignerons de la Méditerranée Réserve St. Martin Cabernet Sauvignon (Vin de Pays d'Oc)
tasting_notes: Here's a simple but enjoyable Cab with notes of black plum, violet and cassis. Medium weight with soft tannins and a solid finish.

name: Familia Mayol Vista Flores Sauvignon Blanc (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Small-production (300 cases total) SB from high-elevation vineyards with solid apple and citrus aromas. Basic but clean, with lemon, orange, grapefruit and nectarine flavors. Good for Argentina, which doesn't have much of a track record with Sauvignon Blanc. Drink now.

name: Château Laulerie White (Bergerac Sec)
tasting_notes: Light, fruity and herbaceous, this has a crisp grapefruit flavor, laced with lemon. Soft and fresh, this is ready to drink now.

name: Two Brothers Big Tattoo Red Red (Colchagua Valley)
tasting_notes: This blend of Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Merlot starts off a bit murky and brooding but then displays raspberry and plum fruit, and some big-time heft. A tad oaky and simple, but with grilled meats it should more than do the trick. If you like 'em big and a touch funky, get tattooed.

name: Undurraga T.H. Lo Abarca Riesling (San Antonio)
tasting_notes: Petrol leads the nose, which also deals pear and melon in a solid facsimile of Alsace. The palate is lemony and cut by streaking acidity, while the flavors of citrus run tart and monotone. Finishes zesty, with green apple and lemon.

name: Château Laffitte Carcasset Saint-Estèphe
tasting_notes: With 70% Cabernet Sauvignon, this is a structured wine, firm with tannins that contrast with the black-currant fruits. Still full of young tannins, it will develop well over the next few years. Wait to drink until 2019.

name: Muhr-Van der Niepoort Samt & Seide Blaufränkisch (Carnuntum)
tasting_notes: Lovely tart cranberry and just-ripe blueberry appear on the nose. The palate presents similarly appetizing crunchy red fruit that's pure and unpretentiously delicious, spiced with cinnamon and white pepper and brimming with freshness and verve. Don't let the light body deceive you; this has depth and will develop. Drink now–2025.

name: Tenuta di Lilliano Chianti Classico
tasting_notes: This has a bright bouquet of iris, crushed cherry and mint. A mouthwatering black-cherry flavor leads the palate, with accents of nutmeg and white pepper. Made in a straightforward style, this will pair wonderfully with mildly seasoned cheeses or pasta topped with ragu.

name: Poliziano Rosso di Montepulciano
tasting_notes: This little brother to vino Nobile embodies the essence of ripe, lip-smacking country wine. But it's no piece of candy; quite the contrary, it's full, rustic and fruit-forward. If elegance isn't the game here, then the big plum flavor and meaty, berry-loaded finish is.

name: Castello Banfi Colvecchio Syrah (Sant'Antimo)
tasting_notes: Syrah from central Tuscany? Sure. The '98 version of Colvecchio, an offering from a hot year, is leaner than might be expected and short on dimension. It has lots of oak up front and an abundance of spicy, tart red fruit in the middle. The oak kicks up on the finish as well. The effort is there and the fruit seems sound, but tartness is the overriding impression it leaves.

name: Urbina Reserva Especial (Rioja)
tasting_notes: This rusty-colored Rioja shows funky aromas of leather mixed with hints of rose petal. A good mouthfeel with smooth tannins is suggestive of aged Burgundy or Merenzao (Trousseau), while rooty, earthy flavors of leaves and tea are interesting. Drink now.

name: Château de Bel Echappée Bel (Bordeaux)
tasting_notes: This ripe fruity wine has soft tannins and generous berry fruit flavors. It is perfumed with mint and spice aromas that fill the glass. It's an attractive wine, juicy at the end and ready to drink.

name: Delaforce Curious & Ancient - 20 Yrs. Old Port (Douro)
tasting_notes: The soft, honeyed nose is entirely inviting, hinting at the refinement this wine carries from start to finish. Though not a heavyweight, there's a goodly amount of apricot and quince mixed with toffee and crème brûlée. Scrumptious, racy and recommended for those who like good Port.

name: Capichera Vigna 'Ngena (Vermentino di Gallura)
tasting_notes: Here's a vineyard-designate Vermentino that shows a bright bouquet of yellow flower, melon, stone fruit and citrus. There's a ripe, full quality to this fresh white.

name: Henri de Villamont Premier Cru (Montagny)
tasting_notes: This is a ripe wine, structured with toast, ripe peach, spicy apricot and an attractive citrus juice character. The wine opens warmly in the mouth, but then finishes more crisply, lifted by its acidity.

name: Quinta do Arrobe Quinto Elemento Reserva Cabernet Sauvignon (Tejo)
tasting_notes: This is a big ripe wine full of juicy sweet plum flavors and dark dense tannins. It is still young with a bitter edge from the toasty wood aging. The wine, with its structure and firm texture, will need more time so drink from 2017.

name: Château Paradis White (Coteaux d'Aix-en-Provence)
tasting_notes: This wine is a fresh, herbaceous and fruity blend of Sauvignon Blanc and Grenache Blanc. Touches of tropical fruits round out the crisp lemon and grapefruit flavors, with an attractive, fragrant tang at the end.

name: Jean León 3055 Chardonnay (Penedès)
tasting_notes: Apple and melon aromas are mild, straightforward and devoid of oak. A chunky melony palate doesn't have much stuffing, while this tastes of mild peach, papaya and other tropical fruits. Overall, this is inoffensive but hollow.

name: Verum Pinot Noir (Alto Valle del Río Negro)
tasting_notes: Scratchy, dry raspberry aromas are standard and accurate for Pinot. The mouthfeel is tight and crisp, with gentle acids pushing standard strawberry, raspberry and oaky flavors of cocoa and spice. Mild tasting but long on the finish.

name: Quinta do Noval Noval Tawny Reserve (Port)
tasting_notes: Dark in color, the wine has plenty of tangy tawny character. It is ripe, full and rich with caramel and spice flavors as well as acidity that is finely balanced. This is an attractive wine, ready to drink.

name: Tour 52 Malbec (San Juan)
tasting_notes: Gaseous and scrambled at first, with leathery aromas that mask the fruit component. Better later on, although it remains sulfuric and leathery, with confused cherry and raspberry flavors. Not much grace or precision, but not an overtly poor wine either.

name: Leone de Castris Donna Lisa Rosso Red (Salice Salentino)
tasting_notes: This is a very pretty wine with lush richness and bursting notes of black cherry and plum. The wine boasts thick, dark concentration and background aromas of cola and white peppercorn. The tannins are tight and solid and the wine would work with braised or grilled meat.

name: Caves de Rauzan Château Villotte (Bordeaux Supérieur)
tasting_notes: This wine has good spiciness, ripe fruits and firm tannins. There is a good balance between acidity from red berry fruits and a dense, tannic character. It is solid and concentrated, and needing to age longer. Drink from 2015.

name: Bodega Las Cañitas Familia Navarro Torrre Grand Gold Medal Malbec-Cabernet Sauvignon (Argentina)
tasting_notes: Gritty aromas of herbal berry fruits and coffee grounds lead to a hard tannic, compact palate with loud acidity. Disparate flavors of burnt coffee, tomato and stewed plum finish with scraping tannins and herbal notes that reflect the nose and palate.

name: Pago Casa Gran Crux Càsa Benasal Red (Valencia)
tasting_notes: Rubbery berry aromas are a touch herbal, gaseous and briny. A combination of choppy tannins and high acidity make for a jumpy mouthfeel, while acid-propelled flavors of plum and raspberry are fiery and long. Drink this organic blend of Garnacha Tintorera, Monastrell and Syrah through 2019.

name: Bollig-Lehnert Trittenheimer Riesling (Mosel)
tasting_notes: Intensely earthy at first, aeration opens up the nose of this rather savory off-dry Riesling, revealing fresher notes of lemon and lime peels. It's delicate in concentration, but tart green apple and citrus flavors are zestful.

name: Viña Casas Patronales Reserva Privada Sauvignon Blanc (Leyda Valley)
tasting_notes: Melony and green on the nose, with an asparagus note. The palate sports enough acidity to keep it afloat, but the flavors shift quickly from lime and melon to peas and asparagus.

name: Case Bianche Tenuta Col Santago Undici (Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore)
tasting_notes: Heady scents of fragrant jasmine, wisteria and white orchard fruit lead the nose, while the frothy, slightly sweet palate offers succulent yellow apple, pear and ripe white peach. Firm acidity and a creamy perlage provide the framework.

name: Antigal Uno Malbec (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Black-fruit aromas come with notes of fresh-cut grass, rose petal and berry jam. The mouthfeel is creamy and sticky, with modest acidity. Ripe, rich flavors of berry fruits, cocoa and caramel finish jammy. Drink this tasty, saturated, soft-bodied Malbec through 2018.

name: Mas Blanch I Jové Saó Expressiu Red (Costers del Segre)
tasting_notes: This Catalan red is dense and ripe, with aromatic notes of beef broth and raisiny fruits. The mouthfeel is jammy and chunky, while flavors of raisin, prune and stewed berries come across loamy and soft. On the finish, this offers herbal flavors and lasting thickness.

name: Parras Wines Mula Velha Premium Branco White (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: A fruity blend of local Lisboa grapes along with Chardonnay, this wine is rich and full of citrus and crisp apple flavors. It is a ripe wine with a creamy texture enhanced by toast from the wood aging. Drink this wine from late 2017.

name: Knipser Trocken Chardonnay Weissburgunder (Pfalz)
tasting_notes: Slight hint of sulfur at first, but it blows off and the nose opens to reveal a rich medley of ripe orchard fruit tinged with dried tarragon and savory spice. Crisp, bright and laden with a patchwork of flavors: ripe apples, pears and stone fruit against a backdrop of earthy minerality. Broad yet only medium bodied, with a moderately long finish.

name: Arpepe Rosso (Valtellina)
tasting_notes: Delicate scents of woodland berry, violet and crushed stone waft out of glass when pouring this mountain Nebbiolo. Luminous and linear, the graceful palate offers tart red cherry, star anise and mineral alongside firm acidity and lithe tannins.

name: Mario Schiopetto Sauvignon (Collio)
tasting_notes: Subdued aromas suggest stone fruit, citrus and thyme. The palate offers yellow peach, tomato vine and medicinal herbs alongside crisp acidity. It ends on a slightly bitter, nutty note.

name: Matetic Corralillo Sauvignon Blanc (San Antonio)
tasting_notes: A full spectrum of Chilean SB aromas are present, from grass to citrus to tropical fruits to vegetal notes. This feels fresh but more or less regular. Flavors of green fruits come with grassy interjections, while the finish is good and clean.

name: Quinta do Passadouro Passadouro Porto Tawny Reserve (Port)
tasting_notes: This is a fresh and fruity wine, full of red fruits that are laced with raisins and prunes. The acidity cuts through the richness balancing the natural sweetness. It has an attractive crisp aftertaste.

name: DFJ Vinhos DFJ Alvarinho-Chardonnay (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: An intriguing blend of grapes, bringing ripe, smooth Chardonnay up against crisp, green Alvarinho. It will work, once the wine has settled down and integrated. It's fresh, with crisp citrus and ripe apricot flavors, all shot through by acidity. Drink from 2016.

name: Herdade da Comporta Chão das Rolas Red (Península de Setúbal)
tasting_notes: Soft tannins and bright acidity give a wine that's ready to drink. Juicy red berry fruits dominate, with tannins just in the background.

name: Viña Vilano Rosado Tempranillo (Ribera del Duero)
tasting_notes: An improvement from recent years, but that may be a reflection of when we're tasting the wine. At this point in time it's showing dusty plum and raspberry aromas and good body weight. The flavors of raspberry and cherry are solid, while the finish is cleansing. Beyond palatable; it's really a nice rosé from Tempranillo.

name: Villa Gianna Vigne del Borgo Sauvignon (Lazio)
tasting_notes: Known for some of Italy's most beautiful sand beaches, you might not consider the resort area of Sabaudia (in the Lazio region) a farming area for Sauvignon grapes. Despite the disconnect, this wine brings together territory and variety with ripe aromas of exotic fruit, peach and subtle tones of seashell and sulphur.

name: Steininger Loisium Weingarten Reserve Grüner Veltliner (Kamptal)
tasting_notes: Generously ripe notions of yellow plum and juicy pear fill the nose. The palate benefits from the same fruitfulness but adds a touch of pepper and herbal savor at its concentrated core. There is something joyful about this. Despite the generous fruit this stays streamlined and supercrisp. The finish focuses on that wonderfully spicy pepperiness.

name: Perescuma Terra Brava Red (Alentejano)
tasting_notes: This ripe, bold wine is rich in black fruits. They cushion the naturally prominent tannins of Cabernet Sauvignon and Touriga Nacional that form part of the blend. It is a solid effort, juicy and ready to drink.

name: Lamadrid Single Vineyard Reserva Bonarda (Agrelo)
tasting_notes: Big blackberry aromas show very little rusticity. Feels full but smooth and balanced, with a nice mix of wild berry, spice and fine herb flavors. Mellow and not pushy on the finish. Really good for Bonarda.

name: Château du Cèdre Malbec (Cahors)
tasting_notes: At this stage, the wine feels lean, austere and minerally, despite the richness of the vintage. But this black-currant-driven wine is likely to age impressively. And with its dense tannins, it shouldn't be touched for at least four years.

name: Dominio Dostares Tombú Prieto Picudo Rosé (Vino de la Tierra de Castilla y León)
appellation: Vino de la Tierra de Castilla y León
tasting_notes: In the mouth, this feels chunky, with sugary red-berry flavors coming in front of a sticky finish. The grape variety is the obscure Prieto Picudo.

name: Zorzal Gran Terroir Pinot Noir (Tupungato)
tasting_notes: Tea, spice, tomato and dried-fruit aromas feed into a lightweight palate with slightly raw acidity. Snappy flavors of red currant and plum are clean, fresh and light. In a nutshell, that's what this Tupungato Pinot is about: freshness, femininity and dried red fruits. Drink through 2019.

name: Lusco Albariño (Rías Baixas)
tasting_notes: Very clean and clear, and even though it's a 2009 it is still holding onto its core freshness and character. White fruits and flower blossoms work the nose, and the palate is now fully mature, elegant and smooth. Flavors of peach, melon and kiwi are clean and tasty. Albariño at its best.

name: Salentein Reserve Malbec (Valle de Uco)
tasting_notes: Earthy black-fruit and spice aromas are clean and welcoming, while this is potent and full of life on the palate. Black cherry, coffee and chocolate flavors are intense and finish with a notable amount of minty menthol character. Drink through 2019.

name: Montes Alpha Carmenère (Colchagua Valley)
tasting_notes: Classic Carmenère aromas of spiced blackberry, olive, herbs and cola hint at green, but in the mouth this warm-vintage wine is ripe, lush and layered, with resiny oak. Flavors of cola, vanilla, blackberry and black cherry are nicely herbal, while a spicy finish brings char and coffee notes along with plush weight. Drink through 2018.

name: Fiuza Alvarinho (Tejo)
tasting_notes: In the Tejo region, Alvarinho loses its specific mineral and ripe creamy texture. What is has instead is intense fruitiness. Green and white fruits fill the glass with a fresh and youthful character. It's bright, crisp and ready to drink now.

name: Umani Ronchi Vecchie Vigne (Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico Superiore)
appellation: Verdicchio dei Castelli di Jesi Classico Superiore
tasting_notes: Made from 40-year-old vines, this structured white opens with aromas of pressed chamomile, Spanish broom and a waft of dried apricot. The full-bodied palate offers baked apple, mature peach and dried herb. This shows some of the heat of the vintage, so enjoy soon to capture freshness.

name: José Pariente Verdejo (Rueda)
tasting_notes: Fresh, perky, sweaty and citric on the nose, which all creates a textbook bouquet. The palate is slightly spritzy, with flavors of passionfruit, pineapple and sweet white grapefruit. Fresh yet a little fleshy, with a long, zesty finish. Drink as soon as possible to capture the essence of a fine vintage.

name: Fornacelle Semillon (Toscana)
tasting_notes: Slightly closed at first, this Sémillon needs a few minutes in the glass before the aromas become charged. Exotic fruit and pineapple notes appear with citrus and peach accents. The finish is simple and fresh.

name: Adega Mãe Viognier (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: This is a wood-fermented wine, spicy and lightly perfumed. The wood aging does dominate the yellow fruits and acidity that still need time. Drink this wine from late 2017.

name: Château Bessan Ségur Médoc
tasting_notes: Dense and dark in color, this wine has a black currant flavor. The tannins are ripe and soft, and the texture has a fresh lilt to it from the acidity and fruitiness. Only on the finish do the youthful tannins show, promising medium-term aging.

name: Domaine de Gensac Pirouette White (Gers)
tasting_notes: The wine is ripe, rich with full apricot and red apple fruits. It shows a creamy wood-laden character that is spicy and toasty. It's very ready to drink.

name: Peña Roble Ribera del Duero
tasting_notes: Full, roasted and earthy on the nose, with only some coconut and berry aromas to sweeten things up. Tight, level and structured in the mouth, with roasted raspberry and plum along with oaky, buttery, smoky accents that confirm the wine's “roble” designation. Good but with some excess oak to process.

name: René Muré Steinstuck Sylvaner (Alsace)
tasting_notes: Although the wine is dry, it has a delicate softness that gives a broad spice and fruit character. The acidity is already well integrated into the ripe texture. It's not a wine for aging, but for drinking now as an apéritif.

name: Calcu Rosé (Colchagua Valley)
tasting_notes: Pink and light, with a sharp nose that's sweaty and sour. The palate is quite strong in acidity, so there's razor-like sharpness and spiky flavors of grapefruit and early season red plums. Overly zesty and tart; made from Malbec, Syrah and Petit Verdot.

name: Vignaioli del Morellino di Scansano Sicomoro Riserva (Morellino di Scansano)
tasting_notes: Aromas of roasted coffee bean, mature, black-skinned fruit and scorched earth lead the nose. The one-dimensional palate offers ripe black cherry, plum, espresso, vanilla and a confectionary note alongside round tannins.

name: Feudi di San Gregorio Greco di Tufo
tasting_notes: Feudi di San Gregorio's distinctive take on the indigenous Greco variety favors a more saturated and concentrated style. The color  is slightly more golden and intense and the aromas reveal ripe melon, honey, dried hay and almond.

name: Château d'Arce Castillon Côtes de Bordeaux
tasting_notes: Taking its name from the Chevaliers d'Arce who guarded this land in the 12th and 13th centuries, the small property is now under the watchful eye of Sylviane Garcin-Cathiard. This wine is still young and just balancing out. Firm tannins are shot through with ripe berry fruits and with crisp acidity. It is a wine that is will mature well, so drink from 2019 and consider this property a rising star.

name: Aldegheri le Pietre White (Veronese)
tasting_notes: Here's a no fuss wine for everyday dinners with loads of fresh fruit, kiwi, pineapple and a strong emphasis on floral fragrances. The flavors focus on dried fruit, sun-dried apple chips in particular.

name: Allegrini Soave
tasting_notes: Here's an enjoyable Soave from one of the Veneto's most renowned Amarone producers. It shows a pretty fragrance of white spring flowers and melon while the palate boasts juicy cantaloup and pear. It finishes fresh and crisp.

name: La Cave des Vignerons de Pfaffenheim Pfaff Tradition Riesling (Alsace)
producer: La Cave des Vignerons de Pfaffenheim
tasting_notes: Fresh red apple and tangy mandarin flavors unite in a fruity and fun combo. The palate is equally fruit-driven and refreshing, with bright but ripe acidity. This is a light-footed summer apéritif and very moreish.

name: Marrenon Capella Syrah-Grenache (Ventoux)
tasting_notes: This dark-hued blend of Syrah and Grenache shows ample length and suppleness to go along with aromas of fresh herbs, black cherries, espresso and black olives. It'd be a fine casual pairing for burgers or pizza.

name: TerraNoble Reserva Terroir El Algarrobo Sauvignon Blanc (Casablanca Valley)
tasting_notes: A note of grass blends with tropical aromas centered on passion fruit. Tangy, tight and citric, this offers flavors of green apple, tangerine, lemon and passion fruit. A light streak of green works its way onto the finish.

name: Portal del Priorat Gotes del Montsant Carignan-Grenache (Montsant)
tasting_notes: Aromas of wet cement, plum, blueberry and cherry come with moderate oak. This feels wide and grabby, with no definitive focal point. Spicy earthy slightly exotic berry and plum flavors finish with grabby tannins and juicy acidity.

name: noblet Côtes de Bourg
tasting_notes: Full of young fruit in its 70% Merlot and 30% Cabernet Sauvignon blend, this wine is just starting out. It's bright with black-currant flavors and attractive acidity, with the fruit just supported by tannins. Drink from 2017. A member of Alliance Bourg.

name: Campolargo Vinha do Putto Red (Bairrada)
tasting_notes: Ripe and fruity, this wine is all red fruits and soft tannins that make it rich and open. Made to be drunk young, it's perfect to drink now.

name: Cascina Morassino Morassino (Barbaresco)
tasting_notes: Balsamic aromas, leather, truffle, soil and ripe berry scents take center stage. The chewy, structured palate offers succulent Morello cherry, fleshy raspberry and cake spice alongside firm, fine-grained tannins. A star anise note closes the finish. Drink 2018–2025.

name: Château Bélingard Réserve (Monbazillac)
tasting_notes: Considerable noble rot both in its aromas and in its palate give this wine richness and a textured, sweet and dry character. Honeyed with bitter marmalade and dried apricot flavors , it is still young. Drink from 2017.

name: Baron Philippe de Rothschild Mouton Cadet (Bordeaux)
tasting_notes: A raw-edged wine, with dusty tannins and blackberry fruits and sawdust wood flavors that don't quite gel, and some green asparagus flavors to finish.

name: Paul Cheneau Blanc de Blancs Brut Chardonnay (Penedès)
tasting_notes: Starts out with some earthy, toasty and minerally aromas, with a streak of minty anise. This is a very full-bodied wine, loaded with earthy, mushroomy flavors, like biting into a heaping handful of mulch. It's also very dry, clean and organized enough to call a good value.

name: Muri-Gries Lagrein Kretzer Rosé (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: The bouquet is marked by a steady stream of bright raspberry, rose, wild berry and bitter almond. It's sassy crispness on the finish should pair well with cheese or mayonnaise-based appetizers.

name: Jean-Luc Colombo Les Abeilles Red (Côtes du Rhône)
tasting_notes: This is a pretty, nicely balanced Rhône for immediate consumption. Attractive aromas of cherries, with hints of cocoa and cinnamon, give way to similar flavors couched in supple tannins. It's not a rustic powerhouse, but a surprisingly silky blend of 50% Grenache, 30% Syrah and 20% Mourvèdre.

name: Château Phélan-Ségur Saint-Estèphe
tasting_notes: Fresh berry fruits, light tannins and stalky black currants, sustained by tannins. It is juicy, the wood a mist in the bright fruit flavors. There is some aging potential, maybe 4–5 years.

name: Les Trois Couronnes Gigondas
tasting_notes: A fresh, appealing example of Gigondas, with mouth-watering cherry fruit that's blissfully uncomplicated yet satisfying for its verve and intensity. A hint of cocoa sneaks in on the finish. Drink it over the next few years.

name: Maculan Brentino Red (Veneto)
tasting_notes: A blend of Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon, this has bright cherry fruit, with light touches of spice and toasted almond. The simple, but velvety mouthfeel will work with curry chicken or spicy beef.

name: Baronet Familia Reyes Reserva (Rioja)
tasting_notes: Dusty earthy cherry and plum aromas are a bit spicy, while this feels blocky, with rubbery tannins. Spicy herbal plum and raspberry flavors show a mild green note on the finish.

name: Casa Montes Ampakama Viognier (San Juan)
tasting_notes: Aromas of candle wax, corn and sweat are funky and oily. Speaking of oily, the texture on this Viognier is just that, while sharp acidity and heavily extracted pyrazines make this fiery. A mash-up of citrus and nectarine flavors turn slightly bitter in front of a monotonous finish.

name: Monterebro Blanco Sauvignon Blanc (Jumilla)
tasting_notes: Jumilla is a red-wine region, but this Sauvignon Blanc is a citrusy example of a tastyquaffable white from the area. Aromas of citrus peel are mildly pyrazinic, while this feels plump and balanced, but with spritz. Core citrus flavors come with a sprinkle of salt.

name: Marchesi Gondi Mazzaferrata Cabernet Sauvignon (Colli della Toscana Centrale)
tasting_notes: Toasted notes of almond and spice give this expression of Cabernet Sauvignon momentum and density. Blackberry, moist earth and tobacco aromas make up the generous bouquet.

name: MandraRossa Pinot Grigio (Sicilia)
tasting_notes: Fresh floral and peach-like aromas emerge from the nose of this pristine expression of Pinot Grigio from sunny Sicily. You'll get aromas of chopped herb, lemon and yellow rose. The mouthfeel is zesty and bright. Highly recommended at this low price.

name: Tritano Montepulciano d'Abruzzo
tasting_notes: Here's an easy drinking wine that opens with aromas of tilled soil and ripe, dark fruit. The palate offers blackberry and plum flavors, with a hint of spice and round, soft tannins.

name: Sauvion Brut Rosé Sparkling (Crémant de Loire)
tasting_notes: An attractive pale pink wine that has bright red currant fruits, crisp acidity and a lively mousse. It is so fresh, fruity and deliciously crisp and refreshing. The aftertaste is light, bright and full of acidity.

name: Villa Rubini Sauvignon (Colli Orientali del Friuli)
tasting_notes: This Sauvignon from northern Italy offers fragrant aromas of mango, kiwi and tomato leaf with a distant accent of white pepper. It's an interesting aromatic ensemble that ultimately has more impact on the nose than it does in the mouth.

name: Cruz Alta Reserve Cabernet Sauvignon (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Earthy leathery berry and briar patch aromas are a touch tomatoey. This feels sturdy, but that's really all you can say about the mouthfeel. Peppery spicy red-berry flavors are a bit grassy on the finish.

name: Ramón Bilbao Reserva (Rioja)
tasting_notes: Opens somewhat clipped and choppy, with citrusy aromas mixed with red fruits. The palate is healthy, lean and acidic, with bright plum and berry flavors softened by some creamy vanilla. A solid wine with punch, acidity and a good finish.

name: Vall Llach Embruix Red (Priorat)
tasting_notes: Chunky, fruity and softer than many Priorat wines. There's raisin, blackberry and prune on the nose, which is followed by a grippy, round palate with sweet blackberry, raisin and chocolate flavors. Fleshy and easy on the finish, with coconut and warmth. Drink now through 2014.

name: Winzer Krems Sandgrube 13 Rosé Zweigelt (Niederösterreich)
tasting_notes: A deliciously fragrant, fresh wine, bright and lively. It has intense, tangy acidity that cuts right through red currant and raspberry fruit flavors. Ready to go now. Screwcap.

name: Agostina Pieri Brunello di Montalcino
tasting_notes: Aromas suggest toast, mocha, vanilla, dark-skinned fruit and a whiff of burnt matches. The oak-driven spices carry over to the palate along with a licorice note but not much fruit richness. Astringent tannins provide the backbone.

name: Mayu Carmenère-Syrah (Elqui Valley)
tasting_notes: Stalky, jumbled, saucy aromas of jammy red fruits are all over the map. This Elqui Valley blend feels creamy and jammy, while syrupy, herbal-tasting raspberry and stewed cherry flavors finish with oaky notes of vanilla and heat.

name: Henri Schoenheitz Holder Pinot Gris (Alsace)
tasting_notes: The granite soil of the Holder vineyard lends itself to Pinot Gris, allowing the grapes to keep freshness while adding a rich undertow. This wine is full in the mouth, medium sweet in style and generous. It will age over the short-term, so drink from 2016.

name: Casa de Vila Verde Tiroliro White (Vinho Verde)
tasting_notes: The wine is off dry, fruity and refreshing. It has lively citrus acidity as well as sliced apple crispness. The wine has the lightest prickle on the tongue, leaving a bright aftertaste. Drink now.

name: Portal Del Alto Reserva Cabernet Sauvignon (Maipo Valley)
tasting_notes: This is a well-made wine, correct in all respects but decidely light for a Cabernet Sauvignon, perhaps a reflection of the difficult 1998 (La Niña) vintage. However, its attractive flavor package and appraochable structure make for easy drinking with tonight's pasta or pizza.

name: Vilarnau Brut Rosé Red (Cava)
tasting_notes: Orange and nectarine aromas carry the nose to a wide, fairly acidic palate that still manages to fall a little flat in terms of character. Mid-tier notes of orange and stone fruit set up a finish with similar flavors.

name: Naia Las Brisas White (Rueda)
tasting_notes: Floral, whitefruit aromas are mild on the nose. Citrus, melon and tropical fruit flavors ride on a balanced palate showing brightness without being sharp or scouring. The weighty finish of this Verdejo, Viura, and Sauvignon Blanc blend shows presence but isn't too heavy.

name: Casa Santos Lima Lab Red (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: With partial aging in wood, this is a spicy, smoky wine that is also full of ripe red fruits. Well-integrated tannins give shape to this wine. A crisp aftertaste and the wine is ready to drink.

name: Rui Roboredo Madeira Beyra Colheita Tinto Red (Beira Interior)
tasting_notes: A blend of Tinta Roriz and the local Jaen, this wine has both fresh fruits and dry tannins. The fruits are going to prevail, giving red berry fruit flavors with fresh, cool acidity. The tannins will be there to sustain the fruit. Drink from late 2016.

name: Elki Sauvignon Blanc (Elqui Valley)
tasting_notes: Pleasant and melony on the nose, without the sharp, piercing aromas that sometimes push Chilean SB over the edge. New from the north of Chile, Elki is medium-bodied and generous, but not too angular. It's a whole wine with common citrus flavors as opposed to something demanding and sharp.Drink right away.

name: Château La Mothe du Barry Cuvee le Barry (Bordeaux Supérieur)
tasting_notes: This is a perfumed wine, and its new wood and violet aromas create equally pleasant flavors. The surface-level brilliance is followed by rich, dark tannins and a blackberry note.

name: Dürnberg L & T Grüner Veltliner (Niederösterreich)
tasting_notes: This wine has a crisp character, tangy with apples and laced with citrus fruits. It's totally ready to drink. Screwcap.

name: Les Vignerons des Coteaux Romanais La Dilecta Sauvignon Blanc (Touraine)
tasting_notes: This wine shows a lot of spice and pepper as well as the more usual herbal fruitiness. The ripeness of the grapes gives a wine that is plush, full in the mouth and ready to drink.

name: Blue Fish Sweet Riesling (Pfalz)
tasting_notes: Cute packaging belies the surprising depth to this Riesling. It's remarkably balanced, with an array of mineral, floral and fruit dimensions. Juicy, with preserved peach flavors and zippy lemon acidity, it's a thirst-quenching, solid pick from the Pfalz.

name: Pezat Bordeaux Supérieur
tasting_notes: A rich, ripe concentrated wine, packed with red plum and cherry fruits, lightly layered with tannins. The wine is immediately attractive, juicy, ready to drink.

name: Wieninger Wiener Gemischter Satz White (Vienna)
tasting_notes: The typical field blend from Vienna, full and deliciously spicy. It has elegance and style, a wine that waltzes across the palate, offering hints of lychee, pear and crisp citrus all finely integrated by tangy acidity. Screw cap.

name: Pagos Familia Langa Real de Aragon Garnacha (Calatayud)
tasting_notes: Dark, meaty and ripe, the bouqiet has a strong wave of herb and carob notes. It feels grabby almost to the point of cloying, with heavily oaked flavors of roasted black fruit and milk chocolate. This is oak dominated, but full and chocolaty.

name: Baglio del Cristo di Campobello Lusirà Syrah (Sicilia)
tasting_notes: Lusirà is Sicilian dialect for “Syrah” grape and this hearty expression opens with inky dark concentration and intense aromas of ripe blackberry, blueberry, cinnamon, leather and smoked bacon fat. It shows a rich, chewy feel in the mouth.

name: Pala Essentija Bovale (Isola dei Nuraghi)
tasting_notes: Bovale is a little-known red grape from Sardinia that offers smooth and rustic characteristics that recall dried tobacco, earth, black fruit and spice. The finish is long and polished, with nice concentration and intensity.

name: Château de Lancyre Coste d'Aleyrac Red (Coteaux du Languedoc Pic Saint Loup)
appellation: Coteaux du Languedoc Pic Saint Loup
tasting_notes: This blend of 50% Syrah, 40% Grenache and 10% Carignan starts off tight and firm, but with time it reveals attractive aromas and flavors of small red berries and plums accented by garrigue and a hint of sweet woody smoke. It's firmly structured, with gripping tannins and a faint cocoa accent to the dry finish.

name: Château les Petits Arnauds Cuvée Amiral (Blaye Côtes de Bordeaux)
tasting_notes: Juicy with fine berry fruit, this is an open wine that will develop quickly. With its attractive acidity and smoky character from wood aging, it has the potential to be a delicious wine. Drink from 2020.

name: Türk Kremser Sandgrube Reserve Grüner Veltliner (Kremstal)
tasting_notes: The inviting notion of gently sun-ripened yellow plums on the nose draws you in. The palate follows this with gentle, juicy but balanced ripeness, featuring mirabelle plum and pear. There is a welcome grapefruit zestiness to the body and finish that makes this refreshing and moreish.

name: Castello di Monterinaldi Riserva (Chianti Classico)
tasting_notes: This vibrant blend of 90% Sangiovese, 5% Canaiolo and 5% Merlot opens with an intense fragrance of violet, lilac and raspberries accented with whiffs of orange peel and sandalwood. Juicy black cherry, black plum, white pepper and cinnamon-spice take center stage on the palate alongside a firm, tannic backbone. Already delicious, hold for complexity. Drink through 2018.

name: Tenuta Buon Tempo Rosso di Montalcino
tasting_notes: Subdued aromas recall dark-skinned berry, moist earth and a whiff of menthol. The straightforward, medium-bodied palate shows dark cherry and clove alongside bright acidity and firm but not very persistent tannins.

name: Durigutti Reserva Bonarda (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: The color is deep purple, the nose dense, alluring and hinting at mint, shoe polish, violet and blackberry. Flavors are pure, modestly oaky and deep in terms of wild berry, coffee and chocolate.

name: As Laxas Albariño (Rías Baixas)
tasting_notes: Pure minerals, peach and melon aromas come with a hint of leesy dust. This wine is elegant, chiseled and minerally on the palate. Flavors of dusty apple and citrus end long and stony, with class. Laxas is a top-flight Albariño producer and this vintage is one of its best. Drink now.

name: Spyros Hatziyiannis Assyrtico (Santorini)
tasting_notes: Aromas of sea salt, pineapple and citrus start this lively Assyrtiko. It offers a fresh mineral character rounded by tropical fruit. Friendly and not fussy.

name: Lamadrid Single Vineyard Gran Reserva Cabernet Franc (Agrelo)
tasting_notes: Earthy aromas of Boston baked beans and stewed berry fruits set up a stout, dense, ripe palate. This wine tastes of baked berries and cassis. A finish with spice-cake flavors feels dense and meaty, with a savory aftertaste.

name: Emmerich Knoll Loibner Smaragd Traminer (Wachau)
tasting_notes: Tender but rich notes of damask rose dominate the nose. They are joined on the palate by a textured, almost phenolic mouthfeel in which fresh citrus vibrates and swings along with just off-dry notes of ripe stone fruit. This lush but still toned wine will come into its own with rich, soft-rind cheeses or spicy Asian fare.

name: Canella Extra Dry (Prosecco)
tasting_notes: Canella's pocketbook-friendly Prosecco opens with drying tones of talcum powder, citrus and tangerine. The mouthfeel is cheerful, lean, informal and crisp.

name: Gino Fasoli La Corte del Pozzo (Valpolicella)
tasting_notes: A blend of organically cultivated Corvina, Rondinella and Corvinone, this has enticing aromas of red berry and fragrant blue flower. The juicy palate offers red cherry, red currant and a hint of green pepper alongside smooth tannins and fresh acidity. Enjoy soon.

name: Falua Conde Vimioso Reserva Branco White (Tejo)
tasting_notes: This is a really rich manifestation of Arinto. Its ripe pear and apricot flavors are laced with wood fermentation and aging toastiness. Its dense texture comes from the grape selection, while its richness comes from the sandy soil of the vineyard. It is a fine wine, likely ready to drink from 2018.

name: Casa al Vento Aria (Chianti Classico)
tasting_notes: Aria is a stunning Chianti Classico, boasting earthy, underbrush aromas with hints of subdued oak. The palate delivers fabulous, juicy plum and black-cherry layered with well integrated vanilla and espresso. It's still tight and tannic so give this a few more years.

name: Les Frères Couillaud Château de la Ragotière Vallet (Muscadet Sèvre et Maine)
tasting_notes: This is a beautifully fruity wine with great acidity and citrus flavors contrasting with ripe apple and melon fruitiness. The wine is cool, crisp, full of juicy acidity, and ready to drink now.

name: DFJ Vinhos Paxis Pinot Noir (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: This softly perfumed wine has red-fruit flavors and plenty of acidity. It is jammy and juicy with succulent red berries. Drink now.

name: Casa Santos Lima Azulejo White (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: A medium-sweet wine, with a light prickle on tongue, very much in the style of some Vinho Verde, this is crisp, with lemon candy flavors and bright acidity. Drink now.

name: Santa Alicia Gran Reserva de los Andes Carmenère (Maipo Valley)
tasting_notes: Not as dark and sticky as many wines of this variety; the nose is defined by cherry and raspberry along with barnyard and animal hide. At first the palate seems sharp and acidic, but with time it settles on fuller, more creamy cherry and raspberry along with mocha. Narrow on the finish but fresh and forward.

name: Vèscine Chianti Classico
tasting_notes: Luminous and buoyant, this Chianti Classico (Sangiovese with a small percentage of Canaiolo) offers delicate notes of wild berry, cola and violets. It tastes like a traditional Chianti Classico should, although it is not overly intense or persistent.

name: Leira Albariño (Rías Baixas)
tasting_notes: An elegant and well-made Albariño with lemon chiffon, pear and green apple aromas. The palate is just right in feel, depth and minerality, with apple, pear, honeydew and hidden spice flavors. Clean, teetering on lush and delicious as it finishes. Drink this pretty wine as soon as possible.

name: Bodegas Franco-Españolas Royal (Rioja)
tasting_notes: Leans toward burnt and acrid on the nose, yet the palate is fresh but tight and scouring. Raspberry and red plum account for the flavors, while the finish is quick and fades off quietly. Tart and innocuous, but not problematic.

name: Finca El Origen Gran Reserva Vista Flores Single Vineyard Cabernet Sauvignon (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Earthy and ripe, this midnight-black Cab opens with ripe aromas of prune, tobacco and oak-related coconut. A tannic, resiny palate deals rich, heady flavors of mocha, blackberry and coconut, while an oak-dominated finish heaps on a final dose of coconut along with hard tannins. Drink through 2021.

name: Zumaya Tempranillo (Ribera del Duero)
tasting_notes: A wiry, fresh, slightly briny smelling nose sets up a pointed, zesty palate with electric, high-strung flavors of red plum and wild berry. The finish is hard, juicy and a little hot and fiery.

name: Hans Moser Merlot (Burgenland)
tasting_notes: It's obvious from the alcohol that the Merlot here was very ripe. But, happily, it doesn't taste that way. The balance of rich raisin and red plum flavors are well balanced by acidity. There is some smokiness from wood, the ripeness finishing freshly with a black cherry taste.

name: Casa de la Ermita Crianza Red (Jumilla)
tasting_notes: Floral berry and plum aromas are lightly woody. This feels full and edgy, with fairly hard tannins. Black-fruit flavors are certainly ripe, while this finishes bold and intense, with scratchy tannins. The blend is Monastrell, Tempranillo and Cab Sauvignon.

name: Arrocal Selección (Ribera del Duero)
tasting_notes: Dark, meaty aromas of blackberry, boysenberry, herbs and spice pave the way for a jammy, tannic palate that's jumbled in feel. Blueberry, mint, herb and briny flavors finish blocky, with herbal notes and heat. Drink this big-bodied offering through 2023.

name: Domaine Jean Sipp Kirchberg de Ribeauvillé Grand Cru Riesling (Alsace)
tasting_notes: There is something floral and tender, even creamy on the nose. The palate on the one side has a creamy apricot and peach aspect, on the other a totally taut and brisk lemon-lime streak. This makes for tension and interest. This is concentrated and exciting, dry and very, very enjoyable. Drink now through 2025.

name: Geh. Rat Dr. von Bassermann-Jordan Deidesheimer Leinhöhle Spätlese Riesling (Pfalz)
tasting_notes: Ripe peaches are glazed with honey and dusted with crushed stone in this sweet wine that's lush and honeyed yet manages to retain some measure of restraint. A hint of citrus pith on the finish provides balance.

name: Sattlerhof Gamlitzer Sauvignon Blanc (Südsteiermark)
tasting_notes: Grassy notes of green conference pear with incredibly ripe overtones of yellow plum give a fruity but non-tropical spin on Sauvignon Blanc. A strident vein of acidity keeps everything superfresh and lively. Vibrant and full of fruit, this shows what Sauvignon Blanc can do in the right climate in the right hands. The lingering citrus and fruit finish just calls for another sip.

name: Tapiz Reserve San Pablo Vineyard Selección de Barricas Red (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Rich, lusty aromas of blackberry, graham cracker and coconut are hard-driving in this blend of Malbec, Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Merlot. It's oaky and full of coconut, vanilla, blackberry and toasted marshmallow flavors. Ripe and oaky on the finish, it also offers coffee, mocha and chocolate notes. Drink through 2020.

name: Còlpetrone Passito (Sagrantino di Montefalco)
tasting_notes: This dense dessert wine opens with subtle aromas of black fruit, prune, leather ?and spice. The palate delivers concentrated notes of black­berry, dried cherry, cinnamon and chocolate alongside firm, drying tannins that need a few more years to soften. Sip it on its own as a mediation wine or pair with tarts made with dried fruit. Drink 2016–2028.

name: Château Les Hauts de Palette Château Haut Mondain Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)
tasting_notes: There is a great burst of appealing acidity in this wine, accompanied by refreshing red fruits. This balanced wine is lively, crisp and with plenty of flavor. Drink now.

name: Casa di Grazia Gradiva Collectio Nero d'Avola (Sicilia)
tasting_notes: Aromas of ripe dark berry, blue flower and a hint of baking spice waft from the glass. On the palate, notes of graphite, licorice and touch of smoke add depth to the ripe black cherry flavors. Firm tannins provide support.

name: Vinum Natura Bordeaux
tasting_notes: A balanced wine, showing attractive fruitiness, ripe black currants and soft tannins. It's likely to be ready to drink soon.

name: Albino Armani Amarone della Valpolicella
tasting_notes: This big simple red opens with aromas of black currant, cedar and a whiff of blue flower. The robust, one-dimensional palate shows raisin, prune and coffee alongside round, velvety tannins.

name: Brüder Dr. Becker Kabinett Scheurebe (Rheinhessen)
tasting_notes: This sunny, off-dry Scheurebe juxtaposes bright yellow-cherry and plum flavors against a backdrop of grapefruit acidity. Made from biodynamically grown grapes and fermented with indigenous yeasts, the finish is accented by curious hints of milk chocolate and vanilla.

name: Miali Ametys Rosato (Puglia)
tasting_notes: A blend of Primitivo (70%) and Syrah, this opens with sweet aromas of raspberry candy and bitter almond. The finish is characterized by a fresh blueberry flavor.

name: Marchesi di Barolo Peiregal (Barbera d'Alba)
tasting_notes: Aromas of espresso, French oak, blackberry and exotic spice lead the way. The firm palate offers raw black cherry, coconut and oak-driven spice alongside racy acidity and fine-grained tannins. It closes on a note of roasted coffee bean.

name: Luna Beberide Finca la Cuesta Mencía (Bierzo)
tasting_notes: With pure black-fruit aromas, modest minerality and violet scents, the bouquet is right on target. In the mouth, this is saturated and wide, with smooth tannins. Earthy flavors of blackberry, licorice and baking spices finish solid and toasty. This fits the bill and then some; drink through 2018.

name: Corte Moschina Evaos (Soave)
tasting_notes: Here's a creamy white that delivers aromas and flavors of white peach, pear and white almond. A mineral note and fresh acidity lift the finish.

name: Rocca Bernarda Picolit (Colli Orientali del Friuli)
tasting_notes: Extraordinary notes of apricot, peach, honey-roasted almond, dried fruit and chopped herbs come together seamlessly to shape a very intense and gratifying wine. It is creamy, perfectly sweet and tangy on the taste buds and long-lasting. This is one of the best examples of Picolit you will ever taste.

name: Simonnet-Febvre Chitry (Chablis)
tasting_notes: An attractive wine from Chitry, south-west of Chablis, this is fresh, soft and fruity. It lacks complexity, but does have bright apple and pear flavors and refreshing acidity. It's a great apéritif wine, ready to drink now.

name: Companhia das Quintas Portas da Herdade Tinto Red (Alentejano)
tasting_notes: 15% Alicante Bouschet gives this wine its dark color and rich, plummy texture. It has weight, ripe, bold fruit and soft tannins and is ready to drink.

name: Château Vitallis Vieilles Vignes (Pouilly-Fuissé)
tasting_notes: From vines aged between 40 and 80 years, this is a lightly wood-aged wine, with yellow fruits that go with the spicy toast. Full, ripe, and nicely cut with acidity, it has a creamy, smooth texture. Drink now.

name: Château Pey La Tour Bordeaux
tasting_notes: This is an open fruity wine with attractive red berries and concentrated tannins. It is developing well into a ripe perfumed wine that will be ready to drink from 2017.

name: Carlo Boscaini San Giorgio (Amarone della Valpolicella Classico)
tasting_notes: Amarone San Giorgio offers aromas of cherry, spice and clove but doesn't have the natural intensity of other wines from this vintage. It's  more neutral and shy from an aromatic point of view although the mouthfeel is vibrant and crisp.

name: Domaine de Gensac Cabriole Sparkling (Vin Mousseux)
tasting_notes: A very fresh, very crisp wine that has initially shocking acidity. Then, as it opens up, more subtle apple and citrus fruits appear, keeping the cool character of the wine while adding more complexity.

name: Château Fonfroide Rosé (Bordeaux Rosé)
tasting_notes: Tight, bright and very crisp, this is a lively and fruity wine. Citrus fruit flavors compete happily with the red berries to give a bone-dry wine, light and fresh at the end.

name: Guido Porro Lazzairasco (Barolo)
tasting_notes: Fresh scents of just-picked rose, bright red berry, baking spice, leather and an earthy hint of game unfold on this stunning wine. The full-bodied palate offers juicy mature cherry, crushed raspberry, licorice, carob, chopped wild mint and clove alongside firm, velvety tannins and bright acidity. Gorgeous!

name: Sipp Mack Sparkling (Crémant d'Alsace)
tasting_notes: Creamy aromas predominate on the nose and carry through to a round, rich palate. This is generous, full and bready, with a lot of earthy flavors on the midpalate. While there is balance, there is little fruit and lots of yeasty character.

name: Muri-Gries Pinot Grigio (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: A structured Pinot Grigio, it discloses aromas of fragrant white flowers, apple, pear and a hint of beeswax. The lively palate offers Granny Smith apple and citrus alongside zesty acidity. A subtle mineral note marks the close.

name: Tucumen Cabernet Sauvignon (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Pointy cherry aromas initially suggest nail polish and volatility. A gritty palate with candied red-fruit flavors seems generic, while berry, chocolate and marshmallow flavors lend sweetness to the finish.

name: René Muré Clos Saint Landelin Vorbourg Grand Cru Gewurztraminer (Alsace)
tasting_notes: Clos Saint Landelin is a portion of the Vorbourg Grand Cru vineyard wholly owned by Muré. This rich wine is comfortably excessive, very full of spice and lychee flavors. Medium dry in character with a dry core, it is still young and could age. Drink from 2017.

name: Olivi Le Buche Red (Toscana)
tasting_notes: Predominantly Sangiovese, this opens with aromas of wet soil, black fruit, toast and baking spices. The palate delivers fleshy black cherry and prune accented with black pepper, tobacco and a hint of mocha alongside solid tannins. It's reached its ideal drinking window so enjoy now.

name: Tres Exilios Chardonnay (Mendoza)
tasting_notes: Tropical, soapy aromas are yeasty and flat. Flavors of lychee and melon have no follow-through and finish mealy.

name: Erik Banti Morellino di Scansano
tasting_notes: Made with 85% Sangiovese, 10% Alicante Bouschet and 5% Merlot, this savory red delivers aromas and flavors of underbrush, black cherry, licorice and a hint of Mediterranean herb. It's easy drinking and balanced with lithe tannins.

name: Hatzimichalis Domaine Hatzimichalis Kapnias White (Atalanti Valley)
tasting_notes: Vibrant and fresh citrus aromas lead on this white blend from Greece. Lemon zest, orange marmalade and spice flavors on the palate are simple but good. Pair with grilled sardines, mussels, or a fresh salad.

name: Portal Del Alto Gran Reserva Carmenère (Maule Valley)
tasting_notes: This medium-bodied Carmenère offers blackberry, oak and white-pepper flavors and herb, wood and blueberry aromas. Good for a group; will appeal to a wide audience.

name: Vallana Spanna Nebbiolo (Colline Novaresi)
tasting_notes: Here's a smooth, savory Nebbiolo that's loaded with red berry and dried black-cherry flavors. Polished tannins and modest acidity make it already accessible, while a vein of mineral adds a kick of energy to the finish.

name: Roquevale Reserva Branco White (Alentejo)
tasting_notes: Fermented in new barrels, this is a ripe, yellow fruit- and spice-flavored wine. It blends Fernão Pires, Roupeiro and Arinto, resulting in rich fruit, bright acidity and a fine, toasty character. Ready to drink.

name: Parxet Brut (Penedès)
tasting_notes: There’s a spicy tang of lemon zest to the nose, and the wine is made in a fresh, bone-dry style that would go well with a wide variety of spicy/salty/fatty appetizers. But on its own it’s too light and neutral to command much attention.

name: Produttori Colterenzio Cornell Pinot Grigio (Alto Adige)
tasting_notes: A blend of Pinot Grigio with a small percentage of Pinot Bianco that was aged in wood. The result is a full wine with aromas of white flowers, opulent and spicy on the palate, and leaving crisp acidity in the mouth.

name: Quinta de São Sebastião Mina Velha Red (Lisboa)
tasting_notes: A firmly tannic wine, bringing out its cool climate origin. But the wine does have weight and the potential for showing black fruits and dark-plum skins, as well as a dry character. Keep for another year.

name: Ciù Ciù Gotico (Rosso Piceno Superiore)
tasting_notes: This blend of Montepulciano and Sangiovese opens with initial aromas of wet earth and blue flower, along with hints of berry and vanilla. The palate delivers ripe blackberry layered with chocolate, alongside dusty tannins. Not very complex but enjoyable and ready to drink now.

name: Marco Porello Camestri (Roero)
tasting_notes: Subdued aromas of pressed blossom, fennel and orchard fruit come together on this. The lean, rather diluted palate offers hints of green pear, citrus rind and a mineral note alongside tangy acidity.

name: Cave de Kientzheim-Kaysersberg Schlossberg Grand Cru Pinot Gris (Alsace)
tasting_notes: This is a rich, opulent wine with ripe lychee flavors. Forward and spicy, it is showing its flashy youth at the moment. While it will always be ripe in style, as it develops, it will become more sophisticated and complex. Drink until 2022.

name: Szigeti Edition Adele Blanc de Blancs White (Österreichischer Sekt)
tasting_notes: This is a complex, rounded wine. It's texture is soft, rich and creamy, layering acidity with ripe flavors of apple and pear. It could age for 1–2 years.

name: Drei Donà Tenuta La Palazza Il Tornese Chardonnay (Emilia-Romagna)
tasting_notes: This sophisticated Chardonnay offers pretty fullness, opulence and gorgeous luminosity in the glass. Its fruit-forward aromas include ripe peach, almond, butter and pineapple but the wine also has an interesting edge that recalls mint or peppermint. The mouthfeel is less intense than the nose but the wine ends on a fruity, fresh mark nonetheless.

name: Xavier Flouret Domaine la Gemière French Blonde (Sancerre)
